runs.text: The full analysis plan (candidate topics considered, stress test, novelty map, hypotheses, research questions, splits, seeds, fixed hyper-parameters, endpoints and statistical tests) was committed to version control before any model was trained and is provided as the file

. One amendment (A1) was recorded after a one-seed pipeline check and before the full analysis: the emission model of PA-HMMQ would be selected on development patients only (calibration-B and development test patients, LightGBM, mean per-patient absolute error). The rule selected the probability-emission variant (development error 2.858 vs 3.186 pp). The one-seed check also displayed errors for 40-patient subsets of two external cohorts (disclosed in S1). Deviations from the plan: (i) reduced-training-data and window-length analyses omitted Icentia11k for computational reasons; (ii) post-hoc analyses: fair-comparator tests (same emissions, fixed dynamics), per-detector emission selection (R1; selection on calibration-A patients, on which the source dynamics are also fitted, so the selection may be optimistic), exclusion of flutter patients, newly missed patients and tests at 0.1-pp resolution; (iii) one SHDB-AF recording was excluded after the leakage audit (below).
S2. Data processing and leakage audit

Only beat and rhythm annotation files were downloaded and verified against PhysioNet SHA-256 checksums. CPSC2021 records of patient 51 (11 records) were not retrievable from the repository (HTTP 404) and are absent. In Icentia11k, beats outside labelled rhythm regions were treated as unlabelled and excluded. The automated audit hashed every 60-beat window (RR rounded to 8 ms) and fingerprinted every recording. SHDB-AF Data_ID 020 was an exact RR-level duplicate of Data_ID 005 (same Subject_ID; metadata Holter dates 2021 and 2024) and was removed; after removal no recording-level duplicates remained, and 2 individual windows (of 928477) were shared between different patients, consistent with chance identity of very regular rhythms. Patient-level splits were verified disjoint for every seed, and no development patient occurred in an external cohort. The SHDB-AF metadata columns are Data_ID/Subject_ID (not the names given in the database README); patients with two recordings were aggregated. MITDB paced records were retained as non-AF recordings. Windows separated by an invalid RR interval within a recording were treated as adjacent in the hidden Markov model (valid intervals constituted ≥99.8% of intervals in every database).

. Complexity: one forward–backward pass is O(T·S²) with S = 2 states and T windows (≈1,500–3,000 per 24 h), repeated for each EM iteration; FFBS adds O(K·T) for K = 200 samples. The implementation vectorises across sequences by padding to the longest sequence, so memory is O(N

·K) during sampling; the measured peak Python memory for a 24-h recording was 1.4 MB. The Monte-Carlo error of σ̂ (200 samples) was not varied; σ̂ only scales the nonconformity score, whose quantile is calibrated empirically. Timings are CPU wall-clock medians on 4 threads; energy was not measured.
